```{r}
# Load the original datasets
data.2020 <- read.csv("data.ny.2020.csv")
data.2021 <- read.csv("data.ny.2021.csv")
data.2022 <- read.csv("data.ny.2022.csv")
data.2023 <- read.csv("data.ny.2023.csv")
data.2024 <- read.csv("data.ny.2024.csv")


# Function to split a data frame into 10 approximately equal parts
split_and_save <- function(data, file_prefix, n_parts = 20) {
  
  # Assign each row to one of 10 approximately equal groups
  part_number <- cut(
    seq_len(nrow(data)),
    breaks = n_parts,
    labels = FALSE
  )
  
  # Save each part as a separate CSV file
  for (i in seq_len(n_parts)) {
    write.csv(
      data[part_number == i, , drop = FALSE],
      sprintf("%s_part%02d.csv", file_prefix, i),
      row.names = FALSE
    )
  }
}


# Split and save each dataset
split_and_save(data.2020, "data.ny.2020")
split_and_save(data.2021, "data.ny.2021")
split_and_save(data.2022, "data.ny.2022")
split_and_save(data.2023, "data.ny.2023")
split_and_save(data.2024, "data.ny.2024")
```


```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RECONSTRUCT THE ORIGINAL DATASETS FROM THE SPLIT CSV FILES
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Function to read and combine all 10 parts
combine_parts <- function(file_prefix, n_parts = 20) {

  part_files <- sprintf(
    "%s_part%02d.csv",
    file_prefix,
    seq_len(n_parts)
  )

  parts <- lapply(part_files, read.csv)

  do.call(rbind, parts)
}


# Reconstruct the original data objects
data.2020 <- combine_parts("data.ny.2020")
data.2021 <- combine_parts("data.ny.2021")
data.2022 <- combine_parts("data.ny.2022")
data.2023 <- combine_parts("data.ny.2023")
data.2024 <- combine_parts("data.ny.2024")


# Optional: save the reconstructed datasets as their original CSV files
write.csv(data.2020, "data.ny.2020.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.2021, "data.ny.2021.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.2022, "data.ny.2022.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.2023, "data.ny.2023.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.2024, "data.ny.2024.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
